messages:
Anya: Quick FYI — on MistralX bring-up with the Qwen tokenizer merge, we see token-id carryover for some inputs after quantized export. perplexity on lm-eval dropped ~6% on a mini suite. anyone seen similar?:face_with_monocle:
Devon: Saw one reproducer locally. short seqs with punct+emoji trigger it. suspect tokenizer normalization + vocab shadowing during conversion.
Marco: Can you paste a tiny repro? I can try to bisect between conversion steps.
Anya: repro below (python):
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('qwen-merged.json')
print(t.encode('Hello world! 😊').ids)
# then load mistralx tokenizer mapping and encode same input
```
Anya: result: first encode -> [128, 56, 999, 3], second -> [128, 56, 999, 3, 3] (extra EOS-ish id appended)
Jen: extra trailing id looks like carryover from previous buffer or a pad sentinel being remapped. did we run the vocabs through the merge script that creates alias entries?
Devon: merge script creates alias records for overlapping codepoints. maybe the encoder fallback path maps unknown => alias id which matches sentinel.
ml-onboard-bot: Automated smoke test failed: quant-export(mistralx-int4) — sample-collapse: 12/100 regressions, avg latency +3ms. See /ci/onnx/3509999999/artifacts
Marco: I ran quantize-steps with int8->int4 chain and saw identical token sequences until the final pack step. packing step uses `vocab_remap.post_process()` — maybe it appends a sentinel when mapping duplicate entries.
Anya: Steps I propose: 1) run tokenizer-only roundtrip check with merged vocab (no quantization) 2) run kv-cache retention smoke on long contexts to confirm carryover 3) try export with `--no-aliases` flag and re-run sample suite
Devon: Quick check: `python -c \"from merge_util import remap; print(remap(['😊']))\"` -> returns [3] (alias id) — looks suspect. filing a small PR to add an assert that alias id != sentinel.
Jen: Also add a unit that verifies `encode(input) + decode(encode(input)) == input` for a few tricky sequences (emoji + punctuation + trailing whitespace).
Marco: I can take the quant-export bisect — will run the int8->int4 pipeline and snapshot token ids at each stage. hooking in extra logging to packer.
Anya: Good. If packer is the root cause, we can patch packer to strip trailing sentinel when present and add a fallback in runtime to ignore sentinel id in kv-cache flush.
Devon: Patch incoming, tests added. will post link when CI finishes.
Jen: Once we have green on tokenizer roundtrip, push canary to staging and run full lm-eval long-context suite tomorrow morning.
sre-bot: Deploy scheduled to staging at 03:30 UTC for canary run.
Anya: Thanks team. tagging @Marco for bisect updates and @Devon for PR. :thumbsup:
